semantic_correction.stem: A client with heart failure has been advised to reduce dietary sodium. Which statement shows correct understanding of practical sodium-reduction strategies?

options.A: I will compare food labels, choose lower-sodium products, and season foods with herbs, spices, citrus, or vinegar instead of adding salt.
options.B: I can rely on taste to identify high-sodium foods, so label reading is unnecessary when food does not taste salty.
options.C: I only need to remove the saltshaker because packaged, prepared, and restaurant foods contribute little sodium.
options.D: I should increase table salt because sodium reduction is not relevant when managing heart failure.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current American Heart Association guidance recommends comparing Nutrition Facts labels and choosing packaged or prepared foods with less sodium. It also recommends flavoring foods with onions, garlic, herbs, spices, citrus juices, and vinegars in place of some or all added salt. The AHA notes that more than 70% of dietary sodium comes from prepared, packaged, and restaurant foods, so taste alone or simply removing the saltshaker is not enough. Therefore option A best reflects practical sodium-reduction teaching.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Apply practical sodium-reduction strategies by reading labels, choosing lower-sodium foods, and replacing added salt with non-sodium flavorings.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original correct answer was uniquely longest. The revised item directly tests practical sodium-reduction behaviors using current AHA guidance with balanced alternatives.

option_audit.A: Correct. It directly matches current AHA label-reading, lower-sodium selection, and salt-substitution guidance.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. High-sodium foods may not taste salty, and AHA recommends reading labels.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Most dietary sodium comes from prepared, packaged, and restaurant foods, so removing only the saltshaker is insufficient.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Increasing table salt contradicts sodium-reduction teaching and heart-healthy dietary guidance.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone combines the practical behaviors directly recommended by current AHA guidance.
cueing_check: All four options are client teaching statements of comparable length and specificity; no unique-length or absolute-word cue identifies A.
